items.stem: Which list shows the correct order from smallest to largest?

options.text: Milky Way, universe, solar system, Earth
Solar system, Earth, universe, Milky Way
Earth, solar system, Milky Way, universe
Universe, Milky Way, solar system, Earth

items.explanation: From smallest to largest: Earth sits inside the solar system, the solar system sits inside the Milky Way, and the Milky Way is one of billions of galaxies inside the universe.

items.stem: When you look up at the night sky, almost every star you see is part of what?

options.text: A different galaxy far away
Our own galaxy, the Milky Way
The Sun's surface
The Andromeda galaxy

items.explanation: Nearly every star you can see with your eyes belongs to our own galaxy, the Milky Way. The night sky is a view from inside our galaxy.

options.text: The solar system that contains Earth
Another name for the entire universe
A single, very large star
The galaxy that contains our solar system

items.explanation: The Milky Way is our home galaxy. It contains our solar system plus hundreds of billions of other stars.

items.stem: Which statement about our Sun is correct?

options.text: It is one ordinary star among hundreds of billions in the Milky Way
It is the largest star in the entire universe
It is the exact center of the universe
It is the only star in the Milky Way

items.explanation: The Sun is one ordinary star among the hundreds of billions in the Milky Way. It looks huge and bright to us only because it is so close.

items.stem: The Milky Way is best described as which of these?

options.text: The only galaxy that exists
The exact center of the universe
One of billions of galaxies in the universe
A small group of nearby planets

items.explanation: The Milky Way is one of billions of galaxies scattered across the universe. It is not the only galaxy, and it is not the center of anything.

options.text: A single planet and its moons
An enormous collection of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity
The curved path a planet takes around a star
A tool scientists use to measure distance

items.explanation: A galaxy is an enormous collection of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity. A single galaxy can hold hundreds of billions of stars.

items.stem: Why do scientists use models, like a zoom-out diagram, to show Earth's place in the universe?

options.text: Because the universe is actually very small
Because models are always perfectly exact copies
Because photographs of space are not allowed
Because the real distances are far too large to show at true size

items.explanation: Space is far too large to draw at true size, so scientists use models and scale to help us picture where Earth fits.

items.stem: A light-year is a measure of what?

options.text: Distance, how far light travels in one year
How old a star is
The time it takes Earth to orbit the Sun
How bright a galaxy is

items.explanation: A light-year is a distance, not a time. It is how far light travels in one year. Scientists use it because space is far too big to measure in miles.

items.stem: Space is full of galaxies, yet the night sky looks mostly dark and empty. Why?

options.text: There are only a few galaxies in the universe
Galaxies do not give off any light
Most galaxies are so far away that their light is too faint to see without telescopes
The Moon hides the other galaxies from view

items.explanation: Space is not empty. The galaxies are real and enormous, but they are so far away that their light is too faint for our eyes without powerful telescopes.

items.stem: Which statement best describes where Earth fits in the universe?

options.text: Earth is the center of the Milky Way
Earth is one planet in the solar system, which is part of the Milky Way, which is one of billions of galaxies
Earth is the largest object in the solar system
Earth sits outside the Milky Way

items.explanation: Earth is one planet in the solar system, the solar system is one part of the Milky Way, and the Milky Way is one of billions of galaxies in the universe. That is the whole nested model.
